evidence.budget_forced: new commit 39be57fe9 fixes critic #1/#2/#3/#5 and refutes #4; re-review the current tree to settle the findings

chunk_findings.detail: `_param_end` treats the first `}` as the end of `${...}` and never skips a quoted span, so a `)` that bash still considers part of the expansion is taken as the `$()` closer and the rest of the substitution is dropped. For `echo "$(echo ${x:-"}")}; git push origin main)"`, bash’s matching `}` is the one after the quoted `}`, the `)` before that `}` is literal text inside `${x:-...}`, and bash then runs `git push origin main` inside the substitution. `_param_end` returns at the `}` inside the quotes, `_find_body` stops at the following `)`, the recorded body is only `echo ${x:-"}"`, and the `git push` left inside the double quotes is never scanned, so `check` returns None.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_param_end

chunk_findings.detail: `_has_esac` searches the raw string for a bare `esac` and ignores quotes, so a `case` word plus an `esac` that is only literal text makes `_skip_span` enter case mode and swallow the real `$()` closer. For `echo "$(echo case x); git push origin main; esac"`, bash closes the substitution at the `)` after `x` and prints the rest, including `git push`, without executing it. `_has_esac` still sees the quoted `esac`, `_case_end` walks past that `)`, and the body appended to `bodies` includes `git push origin main`, so `check` refuses a command bash does not run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_has_esac

chunk_findings.detail: An unclosed `$(` / `<(` / `>(` / `$((` makes `_sub_body` return `n + 1` (or `n + 2` for arithmetic) when `_find_body` never sees the closer. `_scan` then does `drop[i:end] = [True] * (end - i)` with `end > len(drop)`, which raises `ValueError`. Given `echo $(git push origin main` (and the same with `<(`, `>(`, or `$((`), the guard crashes instead of returning a refusal or None.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_scan

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `sh -c` descent still requires a word that is exactly `-c`. Given `bash -exc 'git push origin main'` (also `sh -xc 'git push origin main'`), bash clusters `-e -x -c` and runs `git push origin main`, but `"-c" in head` is false for `['bash', '-exc', 'git push origin main']`, so the payload is never `_split` and `check` returns None.
